title: China Backs Mexico Against Foreign Interference and Calls to Strengthen Cooperation During Roberto Velasco’s Visit
author: Ángeles Cruz Martínez
content:
_This article by Ángeles Cruz Martínez originally appeared in the[September 7,
2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/07/politica/china-
respalda-a-mexico-ante-injerencia-extranjera-y-llama-a-fortalecer-la-
cooperacion-durante-visita-de-roberto-velasco), Mexico's premier left-wing
daily newspaper._

**Beijing**. The governments of China and Mexico have common interests and are
committed to accelerating the development and revitalization of both nations,
as well as to being an active force for international peace, equity, and
justice, said the Asian nation's Foreign Minister, **Wang Yi** , during the
reception he held for his Mexican counterpart, **Roberto Velasco Alvarez**. He
also reaffirmed **" support for Mexico in its independence and autonomy,
safeguarding its sovereignty and security,"** as well as in its **opposition
to foreign interference**.

> The relationship between China and Mexico is not directed at third parties
> and must not be affected by third parties.
>
> Wang Yi, China's Foreign Minister

Velasco Alvarez made a visit to this country on Monday, where the meeting of
the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum (APEC) will take place this coming
November in the province of Chengdu, and which President Claudia Sheinbaum is
expected to attend.

The foreign minister also recalled that Mexico will host this international
mechanism in 2028.

He also mentioned that next year will mark 55 years since the establishment of
diplomatic relations, which are grounded in the shared principles of respect
for sovereignty, equality among states, and non-intervention.

Mexico has historically maintained this position, which is shared by the Five
Principles of Peaceful Coexistence later promoted by China, he noted.

During the meeting, Velasco reported on the opening of Mexico's career
consulate in Chongqing, which reaffirms "the national commitment to
strengthening the ties between our peoples."

Regarding the APEC meeting, Wang Yi commented that its theme is "Building an
Asia-Pacific Community and Promoting Common Prosperity." During the days of
the conclave, China will seek to work with the participating states on
revitalizing the countries that make up that region and to activate the
process for achieving a free-trade area, he indicated.

After conveying the Mexican president's greetings to Chinese President Xi
Jinping, as well as reiterating the federal government's condolences for the
damage suffered in the Tibet region due to the landslide that occurred nearly
two weeks ago, Velasco Alvarez reaffirmed the position the country has held
since 1971 at the United Nations General Assembly, **in favor of the one-China
principle**.

He recalled that in 2027, both nations will celebrate the 55th anniversary of
the establishment of diplomatic relations, which are grounded in the shared
principles of respect for sovereignty, equality among states, and non-
intervention.

For his part, Yi highlighted that Mexico and China are large developing
countries and also share the goal of building a fairer and more rational
system of global governance.

China has always viewed and promoted the relationship between the two nations
from the strategic standpoint of the unity and cooperation of the countries of
the Global South.

Therefore, there is a willingness to strengthen, in a coordinated manner,
strategic cooperation on the international and multilateral stage, to protect
the legitimate interests of both countries, and to make joint efforts so that
**the countries of the South strengthen one another** , he maintained.
